note: Every optional parameter the compiler answers with no default, each with what the specification states in its place and why that is not a value. For a call an engine makes the answer is the library surface; for a declaration call it is src/core/emit/defaults.ts, which is read as well rather than skipped, because the one category this check used to exclude is where its next instance turned up. An optional parameter with no default used to be indistinguishable from one whose default nobody had recorded, and the second kind compiled to a study with no values on any bar and nothing reported at compile, at load or at run. These are the first kind. Anything not listed here must answer the default stdlib.md states, and scripts/check-defaults.mjs fails the build on either: a parameter missing from both, or a parameter in both. This list only shrinks.

exceptions.reason: The leg is the file's own rather than the library's. With one declared leg the call means that leg, and with more than one, leaving it out is OS3012 because there is no leg an engine could invent (stdlib.md 17.2). The surface has no value to carry either way.
The size comes from the strategy declaration's own qty and qtyType (stdlib.md 17.2), which is a fact about the file and not about the library, so the surface has no number to carry.
The product comes from the strategy declaration, stdlib.md 17.6.
The product comes from the strategy declaration, stdlib.md 17.6.
The size is the one the leg was declared with, stdlib.md 17.6, which the surface cannot see.
The side is the one the leg was declared with, stdlib.md 17.6, which the surface cannot see.
The label falls back to the name the input was assigned to (stdlib.md 13.2), which is a fact about the script rather than about the library, so there is no text for the compiler to fill.

stdlib.md 13.3 names the kinds that accept it and gives no default, and compiled-program.md 2.6 carries the field as nullable. An argument nobody wrote is absent rather than filled, which is a decision rather than a gap.
As input.min, stdlib.md 13.3. A list given is what makes the input a select, so there is no empty list to fill in.

Each row of stdlib.md 13.1 names the control that row is showing rather than a default, and compiled-program.md 2.6's kind is settled by the declared type and the argument together, so there is no one value the compiler could fill.

A gap in the specification rather than a decision. The row for req.candle in stdlib.md 15.1 prints mode with no default, where the two reads beside it in the same table print mode = "confirmed". The mode is the whole subject of 15.3 and the call is meaningless without one, so this is almost certainly the row and not the rule. It is recorded rather than guessed: a default this compiler invented would be a repainting rule nobody wrote down. The entry is planned, so no script can reach it yet.
